what: Incyte develops medicines for cancer and inflammatory disease. Jakafi, for a group of blood disorders, is its main product, and Opzelura is a cream for eczema and vitiligo.
customers: Haematologists, oncologists and dermatologists, with treatment paid for by insurers and health systems.
money: treatment for myelofibrosis and polycythemia vera
topical cream for eczema and vitiligo
moat: Jakafi is the standard of care in its blood disorders, with a prescriber base of specialists who know it well, protected by patents into the next decade.
risks: Jakafi loses US exclusivity at the end of this decade, which is the central question for the company
Pipeline setbacks have forced it to write off programmes
Opzelura uptake has been slower than hoped
opportunities: Gross margin of 93% with a 29% operating margin
Revenue grew about 21% last year and about 15% a year over three years
Cash of about $3.3 billion against almost no debt funds the pipeline
watch: Jakafi sales growth, Opzelura uptake, and late-stage pipeline results.
